summary: Browser extension header injection causes SSE stream split and missing final fragment
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that SSE streaming responses occasionally arrive truncated: the final JSON metadata ("end" marker and final text block) is missing. This occurs only when a particular browser extension (injects custom headers for telemetry) is enabled. Impact: generation responses for long completions are missing closing paragraphs or end-marker events leading to partial outputs in customer UI. Environment: prod - us-east, customer running Redwood SDK for Web (v0.9.7) behind corporate network with extension installed. Steps to reproduce:
1) Install the named browser extension that attaches an extra X-Client-Tag header and performs request rewrite.
2) Start a streaming SSE chat completion to the Redwood API endpoint.
3) Observe that the stream emits regular chunks then abruptly ends without the final "end" event or trailing metadata.
Observed behavior: final chunk never arrives, client eventually times out or falls back to non-streaming result which is incomplete. Disabling the extension resolves the issue consistently.
Expected behavior: SSE session should include the complete terminal chunk with event marker and trailing metadata.
Logs & traces: customer supplied HAR and raw socket dump showing a 0-byte header insertion and an extra CRLF before one SSE chunk boundary; edge-proxy logs show chunk flush with boundary at offset N and sse-handler shows no downstream error recorded.
Attachments: HAR (attached), browser extension identifier and version, SDK debug log (trace level).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Reproduced locally by installing extension (v2.3.1) in Chrome; observed an extra header insertion and header/body boundary shift that caused NGINX-style chunking to split a single SSE event across two TCP writes.

Edge-proxy analysis: edge-proxy was flushing on header rewrite + explicit flush call from extension proxy, creating a split where the JSON end-bracket and metadata were sent in a subsequent chunk that the client-sse parser ignored due to missing event prefix.

Hypothesis: browser extension is rewriting request and triggering connection semantics that our edge-proxy treats as an early flush; this produces a half-formed SSE event (no event: end marker) which the client parser discards when not prefixed correctly.
Confirmed that disabling the extension returned stable, complete streams. Also tested with Firefox where the extension does not run and streams are normal.
Temporary mitigation added to edge-proxy logs to emit more detailed chunk-boundary and content-length debug when header rewrite is detected (INT-4571 created).
Long-term fix: PR created to make sse-handler tolerant of split-event boundaries by reassembling adjacent chunks before passing to SDK parser (see related PR).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Customer): Customer filed report after multiple users saw missing final paragraph in streamed completions. Provided HAR and screenshot of extension settings.
2026-03-10 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Asked customer for full HAR, extension name/version, SDK trace log and whether repro is consistent when extension disabled.
2026-03-11 - Maya Chen (Customer): Uploaded HAR and confirmed disabling extension fixes the issue. Noted corporate policy requires extension to be enabled by default on user workstations.
2026-03-11 - Edge Team (Raj Patel): Reproduced with extension in lab and confirmed chunk split; added INT-4571 to track internal telemetry changes to edge-proxy.

2026-03-12 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Deployed temporary log-level change to edge-proxy in us-east to capture chunk boundaries for affected customer and asked them to retry. Customer confirmed more detailed logs sent.
2026-03-12 - Maya Chen (Customer): Verified workaround: using a proxy-bypass rule for redwood endpoints or disabling header injection eliminates truncation. Customer accepted workaround as stopgap.

2026-03-12 - Engineering (Raj Patel): Merged PR to reassemble split SSE events before handing to parser (edge-proxy PR #412). Planning a staged rollout to us-east; follow-up test scheduled for 2026-03-13.

2026-03-12 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Marking ticket resolved after customer confirmed stopgap and engineering PR merged; follow-up action: monitor next 72h for regressions and add guidance to KB about common extension header injectors.
resolution: Workaround: customer applied a proxy-bypass rule for redwood endpoints and/or disabled the header-injecting extension. Root cause: third-party browser extension injects headers and triggers a client-side flush that, combined with current edge-proxy behavior, results in an SSE event split where the terminal event metadata is sent in a subsequent fragment and dropped by the SDK parser. Fix deployed: edge-proxy PR #412 reassembles adjacent chunk fragments for SSE events and adds defensive parsing in sse-handler. Follow-up: add KB entry with recommended bypass rules and update SDK to log split-event reassembly occurrences. Customer confirmed workaround acceptable; ticket closed.
